note: Regressions of the eval mutant gate's own classification. Each case runs the real pinned runtime with one manifest mutant and optionally edits that mutant run's recorded observations before evaluation (mutants --only <mutant> --inject). The required gate exit and outcome are fixed here; an edited run is a regression input, never evidence. A masked mutant must give a run equal to the control (outcome masked); any difference is a technical failure.

cases.why: The unchanged M1 run shows exactly its manifest witness and run exceptions: detected.

The M1 witness is unchanged, but another case's observation violates the schema (HARNESS_ERROR malformed_observation). A technical error anywhere in the run is never a kill: technical failure, exit 2.

diagnostic.detail: gate regression: a barrier timeout M10's manifest does not name

cases.why: M10 is detected through its named, predeclared barrier timeouts only. One more timeout in a case its manifest entry does not name is a technical failure, exit 2.
M4's predeclared causally_impossible error in in-flight-before-commit allows no other error: a malformed observation in another case is a technical failure, exit 2.
The unchanged M10 run shows exactly its named barrier timeouts and missing evidence: detected.

diagnostic.detail: gate regression: a masked run that differs from the control

cases.why: A masked mutant whose run differs from the control in any case no longer holds its masking pin: technical failure, exit 2, never a detection.

diagnostic.detail: gate regression: a setup failure in another case

cases.why: The M12 witness is unchanged, but another case reports a failed lifecycle setup. A setup failure is a harness process error that no manifest entry can predeclare (the M25 conflict): technical failure, exit 2.
